summary: A 1935 Texas Forest Service fire tower on a ridge named for Wesley Love, now standing but closed to climbers in a Jacksonville city park.

facts.design: 125-ft steel Aermotor tower with a 7x7 ft metal cab
facts.status_note: Structure remains but is not open for the public to climb.

access.note: Public city park; the tower itself is not open to climb.

events.note: Texas Forest Service built a 125-ft steel Aermotor tower with a 7x7 ft metal cab
NHLR entry says the tower remained active until 1970
Texas Escapes says the tower instead functioned into the 1980s until fire-spotting planes made it obsolete; conflicts with NHLR's 1970 date, year approximate

notes_for_editor: NHLR (decommissioned 1970) and Texas Escapes (functioned into the 1980s) disagree on when the tower stopped operating; noted in the story rather than resolved. The on-site historical marker (hmdb.org #31698) returned HTTP 403 and could not be read, so its exact inscription is not cited here. Texas Escapes is a general-interest history site, not a primary source, so the Wesley Love / WPA narrative rests on that one article; a Texas Historical Commission marker file or a Jacksonville Daily Progress archive piece would strengthen it. A draft citation to 'Forest Fire Lookout Association (firelookout.org)' claiming its Texas lookouts list records this tower as standing has been removed: the cached source is actually the Former Fire Lookout Sites register (firetower.org, a sister site of NHLR, not FFLA), it catalogs decommissioned/removed lookouts, and its one Texas entry is Jefferson Lookout Site, not Love's Lookout. The source neither supports the claim nor matches the cited publisher, so both the footnote and the sentence were dropped.
